name: r4-m06
statement: RL added a roughly constant bias toward hold-on tokens and away from wrap-up tokens at every position, without a new error detector, so its extra re-checks land on right and wrong intermediate answers at the same added rate (on top of the base's own mild sensitivity to correctness), and accuracy rises only because re-checking a right answer rarely changes it while re-checking a wrong one sometimes does.
scope: Covers Olmo-3-1025-7B base (with the 3-token cue) against Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (plain prompt) on MATH-500 at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, in the stored T1/T2 texts and in short continuations from RL's own prefixes. The claim is about where re-checks follow candidate answers and how they depend on correctness. It refines the literal 'as often after right as after wrong': result-c4411d shows that both models raise hold-on after a wrong result, so the theory claims only that RL's added re-checking does not depend on correctness. It does not cover the part of the gain from format (answer lines the grader rejects), from cap hits, or from the hard328 set, the T 0.6 setting, the 3.0 release or the Code models. It makes no claim about which weights carry the bias.

explains.quote: Not larger on the 65 RL-only problems.
explains.how: A constant hold-on/wrap-up bias is a habit applied everywhere, so it should not be concentrated on the problems RL alone solves.
The lens shift is the uniform bias itself, with no peak at the first wrong step.

explains.quote: after a wrong arithmetic result, RL-base +0.066 [0.061,0.072]
explains.how: A constant logit offset leaves the base's right-vs-wrong log-prob gap nearly unchanged; RL adds only 0.066 nats to a 0.28-nat inherited gap.

explains.quote: wrong-result hold-on gap at L24 +0.128 vs +0.154 nats
explains.how: With matched lenses the wrong-result sensitivity is again almost the same in both models, as an offset that is not tied to correctness predicts.

explains.quote: base's true ends RL's P(stop) is below 0.5 in 16.5 %
explains.how: A lowered wrap-up prior makes RL keep going at many points where the base would stop, whether or not the answer there is right.
Without a better error detector, an explicit review pass finds none of RL's remaining errors.
Re-checking right answers is cheap: it rarely turns a right answer wrong.

conflicts.how: Both models already raise hold-on after a wrong result, so re-checking is not fully independent of correctness. The theory keeps only the claim that RL's increment is independent of correctness.
A sizeable share of RL-only problems are base cap hits or format failures ('8 right answer in a rejected or garbled final line'). Re-checking wrong candidates does not explain those.

conflicts.quote: most of the RL direction's gain is 24 fewer lost problems
conflicts.how: Fixing wrong answers by re-checking fits fewer stochastic losses, but the item does not show that re-checks are the route; fewer first-pass slips would fit equally well.

rival: RL is a better error detector: its re-checks concentrate after wrong candidates (r2-revise-2; external 2610.30882 reports d' 0.57 -> 1.09 for the 3.0 RL-Zero model on injected-error prefixes). The two separate on how RL's increase in re-check rate over the base splits between right and wrong candidates. The rival puts the increase mostly after wrong candidates: a large positive difference-in-differences D in offline prediction 2, and a large wrong-minus-right gap in continuation after a planted wrong final box in the GPU prediction. This theory predicts D near 0 and a small gap.

predictions.experiment: Re-check rate after wrong vs right non-final candidate answers in RL's T2 texts, as a ratio
predictions.recipe: File: s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (all 500 rows, cap hits included). Field text. Candidates, in text order: (a) each '\boxed{' with brace-balanced content (candidate string = content; skip if unbalanced before end of text; end = index after the matching '}'); (b) each match of the case-insensitive regex 'answer is:?\s*' followed by the span up to the first newline, '. ' or end of text (candidate string = that span with '$', '\(', '\)', '*' and a trailing '.' removed); (c) each line matching '^\s*\**Answer:?\**\s*(.+)$' (candidate = group 1, cleaned as in b). A box inside a (b)/(c) span counts once, as the box. Grade each candidate right iff the equivalence function of grader/rln4_grader_v3.py (the one behind score_v3) judges it equal to the row's gold; empty strings are wrong. Keep only non-final candidates: at least 800 characters of text follow the candidate's end. Re-check flag = the case-insensitive regex '\b(wait|hmm|let me (double[- ]?)?check|let me verify|double[- ]?check)\b' matches in the 800 characters after the candidate's end. Pool candidates over rows. r_W = flagged/total among wrong candidates, r_R = same among right candidates. Statistic = r_W / r_R. Report it even if there are few wrong candidates.

predictions.experiment: Difference-in-differences of re-check rates, RL (T2) minus base (T1), wrong minus right non-final candidates
predictions.recipe: Apply the candidate extraction, grading, non-final filter and re-check flag of prediction 1 to s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL) and to s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base + cue), all 500 rows each, cap hits included. For each file compute r_W and r_R (pooled over rows). Statistic D = (r_W(T2) - r_W(T1)) - (r_R(T2) - r_R(T1)). If a file has zero non-final candidates in a class, that rate is 0.

predictions.experiment: Share of final-right answers containing a right non-final candidate followed by a re-check: RL minus base
predictions.recipe: Files: s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL) and s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base + cue). Recompute each row's final score with grader/rln4_grader_v3.py (the score_v3 procedure). Keep rows whose final score is right and that are not cap hits (cap_hit false). For each kept row, use the candidate extraction, grading, non-final filter and re-check flag of prediction 1. The row counts 1 if it has at least one right non-final candidate with the re-check flag set, else 0. F(file) = mean over kept rows. Statistic = F(T2) - F(T1).

predictions.experiment: Twin continuation on RL's own text. Take the first 150 T2 rows (by problem_index) whose v3-recomputed final answer is right, whose gold is an integer string, and whose last \boxed{} content equals gold. Prefix = the stored prompt + the T2 text up to and including that box's closing brace. Wrong twin: the same prefix with the box content replaced by str(int(gold)+1). RL generates, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, 256 new tokens, 1 sample per prefix, seed 90,000,000 + problem_index for both twins. A continuation counts as a re-check if its decoded text matches the hold-on regex of prediction 1 before EOS. Quantity: (re-check fraction, wrong twins) minus (re-check fraction, right twins).
predictions.refuted_by: difference above 0.20, i.e. a planted wrong final box makes RL re-check much more often than its own right box
